problem: Visual object navigation requires the user to name an object that actually exists in the scene, which fails in real homes where users don't know what is present. Existing VON, VLN and LLM-based methods handle high-level demand instructions like 'I am thirsty' poorly.
motivation: Users have demands, not object names, and a demand maps many-to-many onto objects. Objects satisfying the same demand share attributes, so learning demand-conditioned attribute features from LLM common sense could turn multi-object search into single-attribute search and ease policy learning.
key_idea: Learn demand-conditioned object attribute features by contrastive learning on GPT-3-generated demand-object mappings, align them to vision through CLIP's shared space, and feed them to an imitation-learned navigation transformer policy.
insight: Objects satisfying the same demand cluster in the learned attribute space (t-SNE), which reduces policy learning difficulty. Removing contrastive pretraining of the Attribute Module drops Seen-scene/Seen-instruction NSR from 21.5 to 13.1, and removing BERT hurts most on unseen instructions (NSR 8.4 vs 19.3 on seen-scene). Converting demand to object names via GPT (VTN-GPT, ZSON-GPT) fails because the LLM's objects often don't exist in the scene.
method: DDN task and dataset: the agent gets a natural-language demand and must find an object satisfying it in a mapless ProcTHOR scene. It uses RGB only, actions MoveAhead/Rotate/Look/Done, 100 steps, and on Done outputs a bbox. Success needs distance <1.5 m and IoU >0.5; about 2600 GPT-3 world-grounding mappings were manually filtered.

Language-grounding knowledge extraction: GPT-3 gives ten satisfying objects per held-out demand (environment-independent). Demand BERT feature is concatenated with CLIP-text object feature to form demand-object features.

Attribute Module + demand-conditioned contrastive learning: 6-layer transformer encoder trained with InfoNCE. Positives are objects that satisfy the same demand; negatives are unsatisfying objects for the same demand, the same object under other demands, and mixed pairs.

Textual-visual alignment via CLIP: DETR proposes object patches (top k=16), CLIP image encoder embeds them into the shared CLIP space, and these are concatenated with Demand BERT and passed through the pretrained Attribute Module to get scene-grounded attribute features.

Policy: attribute features + bbox + logits go through a 6-layer transformer encoder, then a decoder queried by Demand BERT + global ViT (MAE) feature, then a 2-layer LSTM outputs the action. Trained by imitation on ~27k A* trajectories.

Demand-based visual grounding model: a transformer-encoder classifier over top-k DETR features, global ResNet-18 feature, Demand BERT and a CLS token selects the bbox at Done. It is used for all methods.

setting.backbone: Transformer policy with frozen BERT, CLIP, DETR (fine-tuned on ProcTHOR) and MAE-ViT (fine-tuned); trained from scratch with imitation learning. GPT-3.5 is used offline for data generation.
setting.training_data: ~27k A* trajectories (avg 27 frames) on 200 ProcTHOR train scenes with 200 demands; ~2600 GPT-3 mappings (200 train, 300 test), LG mappings with 10 objects per demand from GPT-3; ~1M bboxes for VG model; 713K images for DETR; 1.9M images for ViT.
setting.action_space: discrete low-level: MoveAhead 0.25 m, RotateLeft/Right 30°, LookUp/Down 30°, Done (+ bbox)
setting.privileged: none for the proposed method (baselines marked * use scene metadata)

results: On the DDN benchmark the method reaches NSR 21.5 (seen scene/seen ins.) and 16.1 (unseen scene/unseen ins.), beating VTN-CLIP-demand (12.0 / 9.3), VTN-demand, ZSON variants, and CLIP-Nav/FBE with GPT-3 or MiniGPT-4 (roughly 3-6). GPT-3 prompting and MiniGPT-4 are below Random, showing DDN is hard for existing methods.
limitations: Absolute success rates remain low (NSR ≤21.5, SSR ≤7.5), and the visual grounding model is a bottleneck.
Only tested in simulation (AI2-THOR ProcTHOR) with a 109-category vocabulary and RGB-only inputs, and each run takes ~7 days.
Could not test stronger MM-LLMs (GPT-4V, PaLM-E), only MiniGPT-4; ground truth comes from GPT-3-generated mappings.
